defining_need_fit.caveat: All nine required product capabilities for this defining need (no cookies/localStorage, no IP collection, country-level location without IP, no personal data/fingerprinting, EU data storage, EU-hosted compliant by design, no consent required, open-source scripts, EU-only data unless opting into the AI feature) are backed by evidence in the selected ledger; what remains unestablished is formal procurement/compliance documentation (signed DPA, completed SOC 2, DPIA materials, supervisory-authority recognition) that a public body's own gate criteria may require.
defining_need_fit.why: The audience's stated need is a website analytics capability that does not trigger the cookie-consent requirement it cannot satisfy with a cookie wall, and every required capability behind that mechanism (no cookies, no trackers, no personal data, no IP storage, EU hosting, open-source transparency) is directly licensed by evidence in the ledger.

ranked_relevance.why: Simple Analytics' no-cookies/no-trackers design means no visitor consent is required, directly matching this audience's problem that its site may not load Google before consent and cannot rely on a cookie wall.

Simple Analytics is stated to be GDPR compliant from installation and to satisfy the GDPR, ePrivacy Directive, UK GDPR and PECR because it only processes non-personal data, which speaks directly to the privacy-review gate this EU public-sector team must pass before adding any script.
Documents the specific mechanism behind the no-consent claim: no personal data, no cookies, and no fingerprinting, the operational detail underlying the LEAD claim.
No IP address collection or storage is a concrete technical detail a public-sector privacy reviewer would need to verify the no-personal-data mechanism.
EU data storage with primary infrastructure in the Netherlands supports the EU-based-with-DPO structural requirement and typical public-sector data-residency expectations.

States the product's purpose is recovering visibility lost through consent banners, blockers and privacy restrictions, matching the mechanism behind this audience's documented pre-consent Big Tech loading problem.
Open-source, inspectable scripts give a public-sector privacy reviewer a way to verify the no-tracking claim instead of relying on vendor assertion alone.

This vague 'compliant with all major privacy laws' claim names no specific laws and is weaker than the already-licensed, named-law claim (E85), making it a poor standalone choice for an audience that needs precise regulatory citations.

problem_fits.caveat: P1 documents municipal sites loading Google Analytics, Google Fonts and YouTube before consent; the evidence here only supports removing the Google Analytics/tracking contributor (no cookies, trackers, IDs, or personal data, so no consent is needed), not Google Fonts or YouTube embeds, which require separate remediation.
problem_fits.why: Simple Analytics' documented no-cookie, no-tracker, no-personal-data, no-visitor-ID design (E33, E34, E80, E127) removes the specific Google-Analytics-driven, pre-consent Big Tech loading this audience's research names, and E132/E141 state the product is built to restore visibility lost to consent banners and blockers for exactly this kind of consent-constrained organization.
problem_fits.materiality_basis: P1 is corroborated across 4 sources describing 61% of scanned municipalities loading Big Tech before consent and 70 municipalities specifically loading Google Analytics before consent, making this a frequently-documented, named risk for this audience segment.

segment_objections.objection: Procurement for a public body may require a signed Data Processing Agreement and/or completed security certification, and the evidence shows SOC 2 certification is still 'in progress,' which the audience's own disqualifier criteria treat as an exclusion risk.

The researched problem names Google Analytics, Google Fonts and YouTube as pre-consent Big Tech loads together; swapping only the analytics tool may not fully resolve the compliance finding the audience was told about.
segment_objections.answer: Simple Analytics' no-cookie, no-tracker, no-personal-data design removes the Google-Analytics-driven consent trigger specifically, though the selected evidence does not cover Fonts or YouTube embeds.
